## Whitewashed Houses and Cobblestone Streets: What to See in Villa de Leyva

The town of Villa de Santa María de Leyva was founded on 12 June 1572 by Hernán Suárez de Villalobos, on the orders of Andrés Díaz Venero de Leyva, the first president of the New Kingdom of Granada, after whom it was named. Built in the classic Spanish colonial style, with whitewashed houses, cobbled streets and terracotta roofs, the town has been beautifully preserved and is home to around 17,000 people.

Time seems to have stood still here. Declared a National Monument in 1954, the town has retained the atmosphere of the mid-16th century almost intact, with virtually no modern architecture altering its appearance. Its central square, now more than 400 years old, is a showcase of colonial architecture and attracts dozens of artists and thousands of visitors. Cobbled streets and whitewashed buildings add to its irresistible charm.

## Visiting Villa de Leyva

Numerous notable colonial buildings surround the main square and its old cobbled streets, including the Church of Santa Carmen, the General Antonio Nariño Museum, the Monastery of Saint Francis and the Casa del Congreso, where the first congress of deputies of the United Provinces of New Granada was held. You will also find La Mesopotamia, an old mill built four years before Villa de Leyva was founded and now converted into a hotel.

Vinicunca is known for the colourful stretches of its slopes, which owe their appearance to the composition of the rocks. The bands run across the mountain's surface, creating a landscape unlike the uniformly stony slopes nearby. Set high in the Andes, the mountain reveals a geological side of travelling in Peru.

The colour transitions themselves, along with the surrounding dry mountain landscapes, are the main attractions. Vinicunca features on nature trips from the Cusco area, including aerial excursions. Rainbow Mountain adds a natural landmark to the country's archaeological heritage, with the slopes' surface and colouring providing the central experience.
